newsitem.title: UK: LVMH says encouraged by GrandMet comment.
newsitem.headline: LVMH says encouraged by GrandMet comment.

text.p: French luxury goods company LVMH Moet Hennessy Louis Vuitton said on Thursday it was encouraged by remarks made by John McGrath, chief executive of Grand Metropolitan Plc, in an interview with Reuters.
"It is encouraging that Mr McGrath now sees the merits of Mr Arnault's (LVMH chairman) proposals," said a spokesman for LVMH in London.

In the interview on Thursday, McGrath reiterated that all parties(Guinness Plc, GrandMet and their rebel shareholder LVMH) agree there were benefits in combining Moet Hennessy, the champagne and cognac business owned by LVMH, with the spirits arms of GrandMet and Guinness.
McGrath will take over as chief executive of GMG Brands, the name given to the proposed 24 billion stg merger between Guinness and GrandMet announced in May.

"As Mr Arnault is only focusing his interests on the creation of the leading, listed wines and spirits company, he need not have exposure to the upside potentially available through de-merging food, brewing and fast food," said the spokesman for Arnault's camp.

Arnault also wants to split up GMG Brands into four separately listed companies -- food, brewing, fast food and drinks -- but Guinness and GrandMet strongly rebuffed this plan, arguing it would incur a tax charge of 1.5 billion stg and destroy shareholder value.

"The rationale for combining these businesses and therefore the most tax efficient time to effect a demerger, is likely to form the dialogue between the shareholders and management of GrandMet and Guinness in the weeks to come," said the LVMH spokesman.
Arnault returned to London on Thursday in an effort to persuade major Guinness and GrandMet shareholders that his proposal was better than GMG Brands.
Industry sources said he was meeting Schroders Plc and the Prudential Corp, but could not say who else.
